articleTitle: Dual-Hop NOMA Relaying System For FSO/RF Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: - this work presents a hybrid free space optical (FSO) and radio frequency (RF) system which solves the major challenges faced by wireless communication system. We consider a base station (BS) communicating to a far across relay via a FSO channel and further relay is connected to multiple users via a RF channel for a downlink communication system. This work is an attempt to solve the interference problem faced at the multi-user receiver terminal using non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). The fading distribution function of Malaga and Nakagami-m is being employed on FSO and RF channel respectively. A Decode and Forward (AD) relaying system is investigated for Intensity Modulation/ Direct Detection (IM/DD) under FSO pointing error. The performance of system is evaluated by calculating end-to-end outage probability using Meijer-G function. The behavior of system is further evaluated at high SNR values through asymptotic analysis. This cooperative power domainNOMA system shows considerable results.

articleTitle: An End-to-End Open-Source LoRaWAN System: Design, Implementation, and Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: As the most popular non-cellular network based solution for long distance IoT connectivity, LoRaWAN networks are being deployed ubiquitously worldwide. While commercial LoRaWAN networks rely on LoRa Alliance certified equipment, there is a surge of interest among the research community in developing open-source based implementations. In this paper, we present gr-lorawan_sdr, an end-to-end system-level opensource LoRaWAN prototype that we have developed based on SDR, GNU Radio, ChirpStack, InflxDB, and Node-RED. The implemented testbed contains multiple end-devices, a gateway, three virtual machines for network management, a database, and a user interface. Through experiments, we demonstrate the operability and assess the performance of our prototype system.

articleTitle: Sensing Coverage Enhancement of Cellular Networks Via Mutual Interference Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper explores sensing coverage in Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. We formulate the sensing optimization problem as a linearly constrained binary quadratic programming instance, accounting for mutual interference among base stations. Semi-definite relaxation based branch and bound method and successive convex approximation method are developed respectively for homogeneous and heterogeneous networks. The sensing coverage of any given network topology can ultimately be obtained. Numerical results demonstrate the tremendous gains of collaboration, and the feasibility of nearoptimal performance attainment with limited number of collaborating base station inputs.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics and Quality Improvement in Millimeter-Wave Communication for Ultra-High-Speed Maglev Train
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: A 40-GHz-band millimeter-wave communication system has been developed for an ultra-high-speed magnetic levitation (Maglev) train, which normally runs at a maximum speed of $500 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ and mostly operate in tunnels. Under these propagation conditions, there are some significant quality deterioration factors, such as a frequency shift due to the Doppler effect and a drop of receiving electric field intensity due to fading. This paper presents the system configuration and methods for quality improvement against the Doppler effect and fading. These features and methods are based on the railway’s characteristics of linear wireless coverage. Experiments on the Yamanashi Maglev Line confirmed that the bit error rate (BER) was reduced to around $10^{-4}$.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Approach for Detecting Copy-Move Forgery in Digital Images
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Copying and pasting a portion of the same image to hide another portion is the most common method of fraudulent image enhancement. Cloning a restricted portion of an image and pasting it once or more inside a comparable picture is known as copy-move image forgery (CMF). The procedure aims to highlight or hide a certain aspect in the finished picture, usually a person or an object. The harm brought about by the horrible deed frequently takes unexpected forms. For the automated identification of CMF, the paper proposes a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) approach. The CASIA 2.0 dataset’s, which includes both real and fake photos, was used in the study. The proposed model is simple to use, and its application shows that it is faster than previous approaches that are now regarded as state of the art. The results show that, when compared to the other currently available methods, the recommended approach achieves the highest level of accuracy ($\mathbf{90.56 \%}$).

articleTitle: HR-net And Modified Link-net B7 Algorithm For Prediction Of Acne Types
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Acne is a persistent skin disorder affecting children aged 12-25. Traditional methods for identifying acne include manual counting and diagnosis, which can lead to incorrect results. To address this, an automated application has been developed using a dataset of skin disease images. The prepossessed images are segmented using the Modified Link Net-B7 to eliminate noise and correctly categorize acne images. The Acne type prediction is then forecast using the HR-Net algorithm. The proposed approach has achieved performance accuracy of 85.74%.

articleTitle: Enhanced Security Framework For MQTT Protocol Based IoT Network Using Quantum Key Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) networks proliferate, ensuring secure and efficient communication becomes increasingly critical. This paper introduces an enhanced security framework for the MQTT protocol by integrating Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), addressing the vulnerabilities of traditional cryptographic methods. Leveraging the unique properties of QKD, the proposed framework establishes a secure communication channel resilient to eavesdropping and quantum attacks. The proposed framework is evaluated using standard security metrics, demonstrating significant advancements in confidentiality (e.g., unbreakable key exchange), integrity, and authentication. The research findings reveal that integrating QKD considerably improves security while preserving reasonable performance and resource efficiency, offering a strong security for MQTT-based IoT network.

articleTitle: Sparse Bayesian Learning-Based Channel Estimation for Efficient D2D Discovery and Pairing
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Device to Device (D2D) communication feature in Next Generation communication networks help develop small, localized networks connecting large number of devices. It will provide communication among the two devices that are in close vicinity without traversing the data to any base station (BS), thereby reducing the traffic load on the BS, and improving the overall network spectral efficiency using frequency-reuse. The D2D composite channel is a low-rank sparse channel. To leverage this sparsity, this paper focus on the D2D discovery and pairing using sparse Bayesian learning-based rate estimation, crucial for scheduling decisions that allocate resources to both cellular users and D2D links. This is achieved by first formulating a compressed sensing problem for estimating channel coefficients between all the devices. The estimated channel is then used to obtain the achievable rate for all the users scheduled for transmission.

articleTitle: Elk herd optimizer for 5G Physical Layer Security
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In wireless networks, data protection from unauthorised parties is essential. The physical layer’s security, which is theoretical in nature, protects the secrecy of the data. Physical Layer Security (PLS) is a developing security feature that increases the confidentiality of data transfer between authorised nodes while keeping hostile nodes out of the loop. This research aims to improve the secrecy performance of a 5 G network by combining nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) with massive multiple-input-multiple-output (mMIMO). We have used the Elk herd optimizer (EHO) to introduce artificial noise (AN) for increased security. Findings indicate that the suggested strategy enhances 5G security.

articleTitle: M-Path, Multirate, Proportional Bandwidth Channelizer for Next Generation Hearing Aids
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The modern era for hearing aids started in the 1990s when analog multi-channel filter banks with frequency dependent gains were replaced with their DSP counterparts. The primary task performed in the hearing aid is the audiometric filter bank. We focus here on the design and implementation of that filter bank. Specifications for the multiple filters in the filter bank are closely tied to the physiology of the human ear. This coupling leads to the filters having center frequencies and bandwidths equally spaced on a logarithmic frequency axis. To obtain a distortion free spectrum from the sum of the filter outputs, the transition bandwidths on its left side and right side differ and have a ratio proportional to its neighbor’s passband bandwidths. We present the technique we have developed to form the unequal left and right transition bandwidths required to obtain perfect reconstruction filter banks. A primary consideration of the filters bank is small time delay between signals entering the bank and those leaving the bank as well as the computational workload due to limited available power from the small hearing aid battery. Minimum phase, multirate filters help minimize time delay and computational workload.

Author Keywords: linear and minimum phase impulse response

articleTitle: Optimized Hybrid DTCWT with Arnolds Cat Map Watermarking Scheme for Multi-Modal Digital Evidence
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Distinctive identifier or mark is embedded into an image through the technique of watermarking in order to prevent unauthorized usage or distribution. The degree to which these watermarks are resilient to different types of disruptions determines how reliable and effective they are. Nevertheless, nothing is known about how reliable these watermarks are in actual situations, especially when there are disruptions and malfeasance. So, an optimized hybrid algorithm is developed. Multimodal digital evidence, such as text, photos, audio, and video, is gathered and watermarked to provide evidence security. The provided digital evidence is divided into subspaces using the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). After selecting these Low-Low subspaces, they are then divided into three levels using the Dual Tree Complex Wavelet Transform (DTCWT). Sooty Tern Optimization Algorithm (STOA) is used to optimally select the scaling function in the DTCWT algorithm. Arnold’s cat map is utilized to rearrange the pixels at random to render the image visually unintelligible. The performance metrics such as PSNR, SSIM and SNR of the proposed model are 67.4, 0.91and 0.92.

articleTitle: Long-range C2 Link Experiment in 169 MHz Band with Engine-Powered UAV Flying Above the Sea
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper presents an experiment on long-range command-and-telemetry link in 169 MHz band with engine-powered fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), assuming to apply to the wide observation of coastal areas, where mobile phones are hardly available. In the experiment, we confirmed a direct link from ground station to the UAV with the distance of about 10 km. However, we also found a problem to overcome, which is on the onboard noise.

articleTitle: Acoustic Signal Processing and Communications: Topic Modeling of Scopus Abstracts from 2010 till 2024
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: A determination of major topics in acoustic signal processing and communications using BERTopic, an AI based topic modeling approach, is presented in this article. A total of 3435 abstracts indexed in the SCOPUS database matching a boolean query from year 2010 till mid 2024 were collected using API calls. To compensate for some variability in BERTopic output across runs, 10 repeated runs were performed to find the the topics that remained stable across runs. A total of seven topics were found that occurred in more than one run. Topics “Speech Recognition” and “Underwater Acoustic Communication” were most stable and occurred in all 10 runs. Other topics that appeared in more than 50% of the runs were “Noisy Speech Signal”, “Monitoring System” and “Optical Modulation”. BERTopic based topic modeling offers an insight into major research topics of interest in speech signal processing and communication during the period 2010-2024.

articleTitle: Estimation of Radio Map in the Indoor Environment: Experimental Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Estimation of radio mapping affects the performance of the network. Better estimation not only increases the user experience but also utilizes the network resources. This work provides error and closeness in the measured value and the value obtained through simulation of a few standard radio mapping algorithms. The measurement is performed in the indoor environment in research and development laboratory and its surrounding area. We have plotted the estimated received power, power spectral density of the algorithm and calculated the root mean square error (RMSE) by placing the known point at different geometry. It is observed that the error obtained is competitive for inverse distance weighing (IDW) and gradient plus inverse distance squared (GIDS) but performance of IDW is slightly better in most of the scenario layouts. That is, RMSE is $\mathbf{7. 5 4 1 2}$ for IDW for equilateral triangle placement of known point while it is 8.5841 in the case of GIDS. Nearest neighbor performance in terms of RMSE for the same layout is 13.8719.

articleTitle: Inter-Numerology Interference Mitigation in Mixed Numerology System using Zero-Forcing Precoding in 5G NR System
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Mixed numerology has been adopted in the OFDMbased physical layer of 5 G new radio (NR) to serve diverse services and use cases. When multiple numerologies are multiplexed within the same frequency range, the system becomes non-orthogonal, leading to a new type of interference called inter-numerology interference (INI). This work proposes using zero-forcing precoding to eliminate INI between two numerologies. Simulation results show that this method significantly reduces INI and improves system performance in mixed-numerology OFDM systems.

articleTitle: Big-Data Driven Anomaly Detection In Vehicular Social Networks Using Graph Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Vehicular social networks exchange a vast amount of data between vehicles and roadside infrastructure. To check the validity of the data passed between vehicles, machine learning can be used to determine when a vehicle is anomalous. Within this paper, we present a deep learning model for identifying anomalous nodes within vehicular social networks. The model employs a graph auto-encoder to encode and then rebuild the network. The output of this model is tested for errors so that anomalous nodes can be identified. Tests were run on a dataset consisting of over three thousand vehicles’ sensor data. The proposed model was able to accurately identify two anomalous nodes out of several thousand nodes. These results show that the proposed model could be used as a way of filtering faulty or malicious data from a vehicular social network. The model provided an area-under-the-curve score of 0.91 and an average precision of 0.95. The model successfully identified the two anomalous nodes in 71% of cases, based on the average detection rate across three separate tests.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Free Information Theoretic Learning Based Channel Estimation for mmWave MIMO
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: MmWave MIMO (millimeter wave multiple-input multiple-output) systems are critical for enabling the efficient use of spectrum and ultra-fast transmission speeds required by $\mathbf{5 G}$ and beyond 5G wireless networks. However, accurate channel-estimation over mmWave MIMO systems is challenging due to presence of impulsive noise due to environmental factors, which significantly degrades performance of classical Bussgang/mean-squared based channel-estimation methods. To mitigate signal impairments due to unknown non-Gaussian noise processes, this work proposes novel information theoretic learning (ITL) based sparse channel estimation algorithms, namely, zero attracting MCC, and Hyperparameter-Free zero-attracting MCC (ZAMCC). These ITL based algorithms exploit the sparse nature of $\mathbf{m m W a v e}$ MIMO channels and mitigate the adverse effects of impulsive noise. Computer simulations are presented for the performance evaluation for the proposed ITL based algorithms assuming realistic mmWave MIMO scenarios. From the simulations, it is inferred that the proposed ITL based algorithms are promising for accurate hyperparameter-free channel-estimation for practical mmWave MIMO channels impaired by unknown non-Gaussian noises.

articleTitle: Security Analysis and Implementation Strategy for (E-Rupi) Digital Mobile Wallet Development
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper discusses security analysis and implementation strategy for the E-Rupi Digital Wallet application. The platform DigiRupi requires to be easy, safe & secure as it keeps the details of the beneficiaries completely confidential. This seamless one-time payment mechanism enables users to redeem the voucher without a card, by means of a digital payments app. It needs to be secured from all aspects of Security threats like Access Control, Confidentiality, Authentication, Reputation, Integrity, Accuracy and Availability. We looked at regulatory compliances, trends.

articleTitle: Hybrid Solver Techniques for Wideband Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Evaluating the performance of an antenna using commercially available electromagnetic (EM) solvers such as Computer simulation technology (CST) studio suite has become crucial. In this context, a unidirectional advanced technique is used for simulating a Printed Log-Periodic Antenna (PLPDA) enclosed in a fixture with foam. This method employs a hybrid solver approach, in which the PLPDA with foam (source) is simulated using a transient solver, and the fixture (platform) is simulated using an integral equation solver. The proposed technique significantly reduces the simulation time and RAM usage while maintaining high accuracy. It is a viable alternative to traditional full-wave analysis, where the source and platform are simulated using a single solver or bidirectional simulation techniques. A comparative analysis with measured radiation patterns demonstrates the effectiveness of this method, providing a reliable and efficient solution for antenna design and performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Propagation Dependent Base Station Positioning in UAV-assisted Cell-less Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Enhancing the reliability and throughput of modern terrestrial cellular and ultra-dense networks (UDNs) through unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has become an important topic in wireless communications research. A key element in the implementation of UAV-assisted networks is the aerial base station’s positioning. This work employs the advancements in channel modeling for air-to-ground links to evaluate the system’s throughput in different propagation scenarios. The UAV is associated to the low-throughput users, which are ordinarily served by the ground-based access point (AP) within a UDN. The UAV position that provides the best performance is selected for all path-loss (PL) models, and the experiment is performed for different coefficients (periods) of update for the UE associations between the UAV and the AP. System throughput of up to 120 Mbps is achieved.

articleTitle: Effect of Channel ageing on DMRS Precoding and Channel Estimation for 5G and Beyond Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This work investigates how channel ageing affects different precoders to optimize pilot density in a resource grid. We validated the clustered delay line (CDL) channel model for different user speeds in an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system, comparing the performance of singular value decomposition (SVD) and new radio (NR) Type I precoders. We did channel estimation only in the first slot and employed the first slot precoder for subsequent slots and documented cyclic redundancy check (CRC) failures at different doppler spreads (DS) ranging from 0 Hz to 100 Hz. Low DS showed minimal channel ageing, while high DS required more frequent updates. For example, at 5 Hz, no CRC failures occurred within 30 ms, while at 10 Hz, failures began at slot 20. These findings aid in developing efficient pilot designs for 5G and beyond networks and improve base station configurations.

articleTitle: Simulated Annealing for Optimal Placement of Wireless Sensor Network Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Optimal placement of nodes is essential for achieving efficient network coverage, connectivity, and energy consumption in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). This paper investigates the utilization of Simulated Annealing (SA), a probabilistic optimization technique inspired by the annealing process in metallurgy, for solving the problem of node placement in WSNs. We have developed an approach utilizing simulated annealing that systematically improves the placement of nodes by effectively exploring and exploiting the solution space. We do extensive simulations to assess the effectiveness of the SA-based strategy in comparison to traditional methods. The results suggest that the adoption of SA significantly enhances the scope and excellence of network coverage and connectivity, while concurrently reducing energy consumption. The results highlight the capacity of Simulated Annealing as a dependable and efficient method for enhancing the placement of WSN nodes. This has the potential to result in the creation of sensor networks that are more resilient and consume less energy.

articleTitle: Beyond 5G Testbed Environment employing the Large-Scale Wireless Emulator enabling the Layer Management Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper proposes the radio system evaluation environment employing the wireless emulation technology that enables effective and critical evaluations of the advanced and diversified radio systems in Beyond 5G era. The employed wireless emulation technology can reduce the evaluation costs by realizing the large-scale wireless emulator environment where radio interactions among the assumed radio devices are suitably calculated and evaluated. The paper reports on those evaluations by assuming both virtual nodes and reconfigurable radio devices. Furthermore, the paper proposes a concept of layer management technology that is considered as one of the advanced schemes on the wireless emulator. An evaluation of the scheme reports on the number of link calculations by HW link emulator that reach to 10 times increase in the interactions among virtual nodes and reconfigurable radio devices.

articleTitle: Osteoarthritis Prediction in Knee Joint Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Osteoarthritis is a disorder that transpires when the articular cartilage in the knee breaks down and changes to the underbelly of the cartilage. Normal joint fracture protection for the bones is provided by the slick substance known as articular cartilage. Early prediction can slow down the progression of the condition. Medical professionals’ expertise is utilized to predict severity. In this research, we address the issue that arises when a model’s validation accuracy is lower than its training accuracy. Specifically, we find that as dataset size increases, the validation accuracy of Osteoarthritis prediction falls. We used a Deep Convolutional Neural Network to develop an automatic osteoarthritis severity assessment system using the Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) grading system. With this method, X-ray images are used to predict the severity of osteoarthritis. This study’s objective is to predict the severity stage of knee osteoarthritis in the form of prediction accuracy (in %) of osteoarthritis using a transfer learning and deep learning approach. As a result, EfficientNetB5 provides a prediction accuracy of over $\mathbf{9 7. 4 5 \%}$ as demonstrated in this work.

articleTitle: Manufacturing and Demand Dynamics-Driven Blended Automation Framework for Indian MSMEs
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: MSME plays a very vital role in Indian economy and has a substantial share in the GDP of the country and its exports. However, on one side it provides employment to a good number of unskilled and semiskilled workers, and on the other side, to sustain the business in the modern technology era and compete in the global market blended automation becomes mandatory for small and micro industries. Starting from the first industrial revolution 1.0 to 4.0, the MSME sector in developed countries has adopted technological advancement for improving their quality and reducing the cost of production; for example, making use of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) which connects man and machines through cloud-based technologies. However, in this paper, a generalized framework for blended automation for Indian MSMEs is presented. This framework is influenced by joint interrelationship between Productivity-Quality-Demand-Dynamics and Profitability. Some novel definitions are presented for conceptual foundation of the framework.

articleTitle: Modulation Classification for OTFS-NOMA in the presence of HPA Nonlinearity and Impulsive Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) is designed for high-speed communication scenarios where high-mobility users strain traditional bandwidth resources. To address this, OTFS-NOMA, a protocol combining OTFS with nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA), is introduced for users with varying mobility profiles. While most research assumes ideal systems characterized by linearity and Gaussian noise, real-world systems often involve high-power amplifiers that exhibit nonlinear behavior, significantly affecting communication performance. Additionally, impulsive noise is frequently encountered in industrial, transportation, and other high-mobility settings, making it crucial to consider both factors when evaluating modulation classification accuracy. This study evaluates modulation classification accuracy under these conditions, highlighting spectrum utilization efficiency by combining signals from different mobility profiles. By leveraging adaptive modulation based on channel conditions and employing machine learning to assess classification accuracy across various SNR levels, power ratios, and nonlinearity factors, the study underscores OTFS-NOMA’s resilience in practical, high-mobility scenarios, enhancing its potential for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Securing the IoT Device Network with Lightweight Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Cryptography algorithms play an essential role in technology for protecting against the many threats seen in the digital world. Many research techniques have been conducted to tackle IoT device security. Traditional techniques are typically identified by their high-level computational complexity of cryptographic algorithms. On the other hand, lightweight algorithms solve most security challenges when using standard Cryptographic techniques in constrained devices. This paper discusses lightweight cryptographic techniques for Internet of Things (IoT) devices and provides a complete overview of the security mechanisms ranging from lightweight cryptographic solutions to IoT devices, analyzing implementation of embedded software and hardware technologies, as well as contemporary methods for IoT device security. Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) and Speck cryptographic algorithms implementation on IoT devices are discussed thoroughly for providing device security. Results validate that AES and SPECK are consuming less memory compared to traditional algorithms in resource constrained environment.

articleTitle: Efficient Measurement Methods of Quantum Computing Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Quantum computers deliver computing outcomes in probability distribution over possible quantum states, which requires repeating a computational problem a large number of times. Using efficient measurement methods to obtain consistent quantum computing outcomes emerges as an overlooked research subject. We take advantage of information theory and statistical signal processing, which are widely applied in classical communication theory, to develop innovative methods to reduce the number of measurements needed to obtain quantum computing outcomes. Experiments with these methods demonstrate significant reduction of required number of repetitive measurements.

articleTitle: Optimized Multi-Model Intrusion Detection Scheme for Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Intelligent vehicles are increasingly connected to the external world, enabling functionalities like vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication and data transmission. However, improving connectivity also increases the vulnerability to cyber-security threats, raising concerns about data privacy, unauthorized access, and potential system interference. Due to insufficient authentication and encryption, Controller Area Network (CAN) and external network gateway in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) is highly susceptible to network attacks, necessitating robust intrusion detection systems (IDSs). In this paper, an optimized multi-model intrusion detection scheme is proposed for IoV using multi-model stacking ensemble framework, combining k-nearest neighbors (KNN), bagging classifier, and random forest (RF) models. The framework optimizes classification hyper parameters to enhance intrusion detection. Simulation and experiment results show that the proposed multi-model framework can effectively detect the intrusion by 99.9% on average and maintains a lower time complexity, thereby enhancing overall intra-vehicle and external network efficiency.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Nano Network under Asymmetric Relaying
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This Nano Network (NN) is evolving with a very fast rate due to its very versatile application, spanning from medical to military and information communication to industry. However, the range of communication is the bottleneck requirement of any NN system. Whereas, relaying is one of the most common techniques employed to enhance the communication range. In this research, asymmetric relaying has been employed to present performance analysis of NN system. Specifically, from source to relay and relay to destination Fisher Snedecor (FS) and Extended Generalized-K (EGK) fading is considered respectively, to analyze Bit Error Rate (BER) of DBPSK and DQPSK modulation schemes. It is noticeable to mention that both of the fading channels are generic in nature therefore, proposed analysis includes various scenarios as it’s special cases. Further, irrespective of the specific scenarios under consideration, observations show that an increase in the values of severity or shadowing parameters leads to a reduction in fading severity. Consequently, this decreased fading severity results in a lower bit error rate. The inverse relationship also holds true - a decrease in the values of severity or shadowing parameters causes an increase in fading severity, which in turn leads to a higher BER. MATALB20 is used for the simulation of the results.

articleTitle: Design of Ku-Band Quasi-Lumped Element Low Noise Amplifier for Phased-Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The paper presents the design and implementation of a novel Ku-band quasi-lumped element low noise amplifier (LNA) specifically tailored for phasedarray applications and low printed circuit board (PCB) area. The proposed LNA design employs advanced quasi-lumped element techniques to miniaturize the circuit size while improving performance. The design methodology integrates a systematic approach to component selection and layout optimization to enhance the amplifier’s bandwidth and stability. By leveraging a cutting-edge GaAs pHEMT technology, the amplifier achieves a high gain of over 14 dB and a noise figure as lower as 0.9 dB across the targeted frequency band. The paper details the design process, including simulation, fabrication, and measurement results, validating the LNA’s performance for next-generation phased-array systems.

articleTitle: Techniques and Algorithms for Optimal Placement of Temperature Sensors in an Intelligent Greenhouse with Non-continuous Parameter Profiles
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Agricultural growth is regarded as one of the important factors for the economic development of any country. An agricultural monitoring system provides details of field-based environmental and control services that lead to the proper growth of plants. The parameters to be monitored include temperature, humidity, soil moisture, soil temperature etc. as these are responsible for the plant growth. To effectively monitor such essential parameters, an appropriate number of sensors need to be strategically positioned within the greenhouse. In this paper two approaches, namely, Equal Step (ES) and Equal Segment Area (ESA) techniques have been applied to the non-uniform profiles. The considered profiles have maxima/minima at the centre of the greenhouse along the length. The authors concluded that the ES technique is not suitable for these types of profiles based on the performance evaluation using three error metrics, namely, percentage average error, percentage RMS error, and maximum However, the ESA technique can be successfully applied to any type of profile. The authors have modified the ES algorithm and renamed it as a revised equal step (RES). RES has been successfully validated for non-uniform profiles.

articleTitle: Quantum Optimization of Radio Resources for Minimal Latency Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Open-Loop wireless communication enables minimal latency communication with the assistance of machine learning in various aspects. A typical predictive downlink radio resource access for such minimal latency communications requires real-time optimization, which is not possible for standard classical machine learning and particularly deep learning using artificial neural networks, due to computational complexity. However, quantum optimization introduces a new technology opportunity to achieve such a purpose. Turning an allocation or knapsack problem into a quadratic unconstrainted binary optimization problem, given a quantum edge processor, we employ quantum approximation optimization algorithm to accomplish with polynomial computational complexity, to successfully realize radio resource allocation and pave a new approach to 6G mobile communications of minimal latency communication.

articleTitle: Optimized Cyber Attack Detection in IoT Networks Using Feature Selection and LightGBM
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The spread of IoT networks presents major security issues, especially with regard to identifying and reducing cyberattacks. In this context, we proposed an optimal LightGBM model for IoT network cyber attack detection. We used Random Forest classifier to find optimal features. Then LightGBM is trained on the selected features. After this the LightGBM model was tested against eleven conventional machine learning models. With the greatest accuracy ($\mathbf{9 9. 8 \%}$), F1 score $(\mathbf{9 9. 8 \%}$), precision ($\mathbf{9 9. 8 \%}$), and recall $\mathbf{(9 9. 8 \%}$), the LightGBM model clearly outperformed other machine learning models.

articleTitle: Terrestrial Mobile Testbed Enhancement employing the Reconfigurable Evaluation Environment for the Non-Terrestrial Networks toward B5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper proposes an enhancement for the B5G mobile testbed environment that enables evaluations of the nonterrestrial networks (NTNs) -based systems. In the proposed evaluation environment, harmonizations with NTN and the terrestrial mobile systems are realized by using the reconfigurable testbed facilities that are constructed to evaluate the future possible advancement on the current L5G compliant mobile systems. The proposed NTN harmonized B5G mobile system provides an expanded C-Plane functions by exploiting the NTN’s inherent advantages of service continuity, ubiquity and scalability thereby further enhances the performances of the conventional terrestrial mobile systems. This paper also reports on the experimental results that are obtained on the NICT developed B5G/IoT testbed with high reliability and high elasticity. The experimental results confirm that the proposed NTN harmonized B5G mobile systems provide system performance of both throughput and RTT equivalent to the conventional terrestrial mobile systems without serious degradations owing to such assumed expanded C-Plane functions.

articleTitle: Banana Crop Health: A Deep Learning-Based Model for Disease Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Bananas are a major food crop that feeds billions of people and provides an income to countless others. Nevertheless, they are prone to a range of diseases, which can lead to substantial loss in yield and quality as well as market value. The early diagnosis and accurate monitoring of these pathologies play crucial roles in the planning of disease management and control strategies. In this study, a deep learning-based method is proposed for identification and classification of banana diseases with MobileNetV2 architecture. Dataset: The training dataset used for this model is a large repository of 3012 annotated images, from four different diseases — Panama Disease, Black Sigatoka, Yellow Sigatoka and Bacterial Soft Rot along with the healthy plants. This model was validated on another set of images. The model was relatively high accurate after some small through fine-tuning and advanced image augmentation techniques applied to it. The high-level accuracy in predicting disease in banana shows promise for being a key tool at the early stage to control diseases on plant which helps better management, prevention economic loss and improved agriculture productivity.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Optimization of Relay Selection and Transmission Scheduling for UAV-Aided mmWave Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications offer abundant bandwidth for vehicular networks, however it is prone to blockages due to buildings, topology and other environmental factors. To address these challenges, we propose a novel unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-aided two-way relaying system to enhance vehicular connectivity and coverage. We formulate a joint optimization problem for relay selection and transmission scheduling to minimize transmission time while ensuring throughput requirements. Proximal policy optimization, deep Qnetwork, and constraint programming models are employed to solve the optimization problem. Extensive evaluations reveal that the proximal policy optimization model achieves close to $\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$ accuracy.

articleTitle: Basic Study on FSK Transmission Using Convolutional Code in Terahertz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Terahertz-band wireless transmission enables high-speed communication due to its ultra-wide transmission bandwidth. However, significant propagation losses in the terahertz range make long-distance transmission challenging. Additionally, the development of high-efficiency signal generators, filters, and power amplifiers remains a critical issue for the realization of terahertz communication. In this study, we conducted terahertz transmission experiments under the assumption that the system is power-limited rather than bandwidth-limited. We focused on frequency shift keying (FSK), one of the constant-envelope modulations favorable for power amplification. Furthermore, since forward error correction (FEC) has not been well investigated in terahertz communication experiments, we examined the application of convolutional codes as FEC in this study. We conducted wireless transmission experiments at a carrier frequency of 289.44 GHz and analyzed the results. The experiments demonstrated that the maximum error-free transmission distance for $0.5 \mathrm{Gbit} / \mathrm{s}$ of data bits was as far as 1.5 meters when using convolutional code with block interleaver and soft decision.

articleTitle: Knocking out Security Risks of Smart Video Doorbell Cameras
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The aim of this research paper is to identify the security vulnerabilities in smart video doorbell cameras which are being widely used for home security purposes. This study will identify and analyze the security threats in these cameras including privacy protections, network exploitation, password management, and multi-factor authentication. This paper will not only review the current literature on the topic but also evaluate the steps manufacturers are taking to improve the security of these devices. The study will also provide recommendations for strengthening the security of video doorbell cameras to ensure user data and privacy are protected. This paper also aims to increase awareness among the users about the security threats caused by these devices and also encourage the manufacturers to move towards concentrating more on the security aspects of these devices rather than just trying to embed as many features as possible neglecting the security aspects of it.

articleTitle: Analytical Model for Performance Measures over Respiratory Track
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Diffusive Molecular Communication (DMC) as a framework for modeling bacterial propagation within biological environments. DMC, a subset of Molecular Communication (MC), allows us to study how bacteria transmit signals inside the human body. The effectiveness of the model depends on the chosen deployment geometry. We focus on a cylindrical biological deployment inspired by the human respiratory tract. This model considers the degradation and flow of information molecules diffusing through the fluid medium. Furthermore, proposed statistical models for bacterial concentration f(y) Further, analyse the key performance metrics within this CBD model and present statistical models for bacterial propagation are binding probability (Pb), non-binding probability (Pnb), evade probability (Pe(y)), and the probability of binding rate $(\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{y}))$. Major contribution of numerical analysis to find total number of receptor bacteria at y segment N(y), and Bacterial distribution V(y). Further, the numerical results demonstrate excellent agreement with the theoretical foundation.

articleTitle: Calibration of Statistical Interpolation through Anechoic Chamber Measurements for 3D REM Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Radio environment maps (REMs) have been the subject of increasing research attention in the recent years due to their aptitude for characterization of the radio frequency (RF) spectrum. Their reconstruction in three-dimensional (3D) space has become an important consideration for resource allocation in modern communication networks. This work evaluates the performance of two prominent volumetric interpolation methods - inverse distance weighting (IDW) and Kriging, by calibrating them through real-world RF data collected in 3D space within an anechoic chamber. Through Monte Carlo (MC) simulations, the methods are calibrated using this data and validated two other datasets obtained in the respective indoor and outdoor real-world scenarios, for different amounts of training samples. The results are compared against the previous calibration of these two methods, and the improved gains in terms of accuracy are illustrated and explained. Normalized RMSE (NRMSE) of as little as to -7.1 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: Dynamic Resource Allocation and Security Strategies in Cooperative Relaying Systems with Eavesdropping Threats
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The dynamic resource allocation and security strategies for cooperative relaying systems proposed here provide significant performance improvements along with robust security features over traditional methods. The method improves throughput, energy efficiency and secrecy capacity by dynamically provisioning resources according to real-time network conditions in conjunction with its interference-suppression techniques such adaptive beamforming and artificial noise. The system is quite good at preventing eavesdropping, and it has such high signal-to-noise ratios that there is a very low error rate. The use case results show that the integrated framework optimizes resource consumption while mitigating security threats, thereby offering a trade-off between existing solutions thus solving some of their shortcomings. Our work demonstrates the opportunity for efficient and secure communication in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Picture Quality Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Since the advent of smartphones, capturing images has become deeply embedded in human behavior, evolving into a fundamental part of daily life. Research into human perception of image quality is crucial as people frequently acquire and interpret images. Automation in image processing systems is vital for quantifying image quality, addressing issues like blurriness, noise, and compression that can significantly degrade the visual experience. While image processing professionals can quickly identify such distortions, integrating human visual perception into automated system design remains challenging. Consequently, machine-based evaluation of image quality is a critical research area. Image quality assessment algorithms aim to approximate human visual judgments. Although deep learning has shown remarkable success in various real-world tasks, such as object detection and image classification, its application in image quality assessment is still evolving. The primary challenge is assessing image quality without explicitly considering human perception, making it a dynamic area of ongoing research. A significant hurdle is the lack of images with quality scores, particularly differential average feedback scores provided by image quality experts on a 1-100 scale. This limitation hinders the development of robust models for image quality assessment, highlighting the need for innovative solutions in this evolving research domain.

articleTitle: Experiment of multipath suppression and performance evaluation of pre-coded windowed OFDM system for wireless harness in machine
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper discusses the multipath mitigation method for wireless harness inside machine communication and performance evaluation of windowed OFDM system using Software-Defined Radio (SDR). The wireless harness communications are done inside the metal-sealed space like a box. Multipath mitigation schemes are then necessary due to the high number of reflection paths in the box. In this paper, sheet radio absorbers are stuck inside the box to prevent reflections. Effective positions of the radio absorber are considered. The windowed OFDM can reduce Out-of-Band Emission (OOBE). Pre-coding using the Walsh-Hadamard matrix is adopted to improve the communication performance under frequency selective fading channel. The signal after the unitary transform is multiplied by the Pseudo-random Noise (PN) sequence. Bit Error Rate (BER) performances are evaluated by the experiment using the SDR device. From the results, the proposed pre-coded windowed OFDM system is effective for inside-machine communications. Moreover, the delay spread of the channel can be suppressed; therefore, the Guard Interval (GI) duration can be shorter.

articleTitle: Scalable Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems with Graph Coloring based Pilot Assignment
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-inputs multiple-outputs (mMIMO) emerges as a technique to address increasing users in 5G. Implementing cell-free mMIMO in real-world situations comes with challenges, and one notable concern is the ability to scale in scenarios with high access demands. Scalability can be addressed by employing an effective pilot assignment technique during uplink transmission and considering usercentric cell-free mMIMO. Various pilot techniques have been proposed, such as random pilot assignment, interference-based pilot assignment, and user group pilot assignment. However, the practical implementation and complexity of scalable cell-free mMIMO systems pose significant challenges. This paper proposes a pilot assignment technique based on graph coloring to overcome these challenges. The proposed technique improved spectral efficiency (SE) and performance compared to existing pilot assignment techniques by reducing pilot contamination. Numerical findings shows that the proposed pilot assignment scheme, utilizing graph coloring, significantly improves the $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ likely SE compared to traditional pilot assignment methods.

articleTitle: Entropy- Based Approach in Bug Prediction: An Overview of Theoretical and Practical Applications in Open Source Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In today’s tech-centered world, where innovation is the key tool in the process of achieving efficiency and accuracy in work. Open Source Softwares (OSS) are platforms which give the license of using, studying and changing the code to everyone. The diverse contributions by the users and rapid development cycles in OSS gives rise to the bugs which lie dormant in the OSS thereby decreasing its efficiency. One such OSS is Bugzilla maintained by Mozilla. The frequent changes in code leads to uncertainty in information and is further calculated using entropy which is considered to be a reliable indicator of potential bugs by identifying the complex code areas which are more prone to bugs. In this study, a thorough overview of Tsallis entropy and Havrda-Charvat entropy has been done on some subcomponents of Mozilla Firefox for maintenance of bug repair which can further help in predicting when to release the new version of software for enhancing the efficiency of the same.

articleTitle: Fundamental Experiments on Modulation Schemes and Forward Error Correction in Terahertz Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In this paper, we evaluate the BER characteristics of the linear modulation schemes BPSK, QPSK, and 16QAM, which are relatively easy to implement and resistant to noise and interference in THz communications system with limited transmission power. Additionally, we investigate the improvement in BER by introducing convolutional codes (CC) as forward error correction (FEC). Through simulations and experiments, we assess the BER of each modulation scheme and analyze in detail how much the BER can be improved with the use of CC. The experimental results in THz communications demonstrate that the transmission distance for achieving a BER of $10^{-2}$ extends by 1.5, 1.2, and 0.4 meters for BPSK, QPSK, and 16QAM, respectively, when CC is applied, with the input power of -1 dBm. These results provide fundamental data that are expected to contribute to the selection of optimal modulation schemes and error correction methods in future THz communication systems.

articleTitle: Development and Basic Characteristics Verification of Hardware Wireless Link Emulator for Large-scale Wireless Emulation
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In the B5G era, increasing number of radio devices is expected to significantly worsen radio resource shortages and frequency utilization inefficiency. To address these, new wireless access and frequency-sharing technologies are being developed. However, implementing and validating these technologies in actual environments present numerous practical challenges, as real-world testing is time-consuming and costly. Testing with real radio devices is also challenging for ensuring reproducibility due to environmental changes. Additionally, large-scale wireless systems pose significant challenges in equipment procurement and operation. To overcome these hurdles, a new concept for a radio emulation system is expected. This paper presents the design and development of the hardware wireless link emulator (HWLE), which features a link emulator and an analog-to-digital/digital-to-analog interface that supports up to $256 \times \mathbf{2 5 6}$ links for evaluating actual radio devices. In addition, this paper evaluates the processing delay, dynamic range, and multipath fading characteristics of the HWLE and demonstrates its performance in comparison with a commercial fading emulator.

articleTitle: Image Compression for Communication: Topic Modelling of Scopus Abstracts Using BERTopic
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In the era of increasing digital data generation and utilization, efficient data compression is increasingly crucial, particularly in the realm of image and video communication. Visual content continues to be extremely important in digital platforms such as social media, streaming services, video conferencing, and medical images. Management of the substantial daily data flow poses significant challenges for storage, transmission, and real-time processing. Due to their inherently large size, image and video files necessitate effective compression techniques to optimize bandwidth usage, reduce storage requirements, and facilitate the seamless delivery of content across diverse communication networks. In this study, we utilized AI based topic modeling using BERTopic for a review of $\mathbf{5 0, 2 6 1}$ Scopus abstracts published from 1972 to mid-2024 to investigate dominant topics of research done on image data compression. The variability in the results of the BERTopic model is observed in multiple runs on same model parameters and is taken care of by taking 10 runs and keeping stable topics that are found in multiple runs. The overall topics of all the experiments are finalized into 10 major topics, namely, image compression, watermark encryption and security, MIMO (multiple input multiple output) channels system, video compression, deep neural networks for image compression, saliency detection, medical PCS system, satellite broadcasting and holograms in communication.

articleTitle: Design and Parametric Analysis of 26 GHz Patch Antenna for mm-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This research presents the design and analysis of a slotted microstrip patch antenna resonating at 26.08 GHz for millimeter wave (mm-Wave) communication applications. The study aimed to optimize critical antenna parameters, including gain, return loss, bandwidth, voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR), and radiation pattern characteristics. Various slot geometries and configurations were investigated on a rectangular patch surrounded by ring, with a co-axial feedline. The dimensional parameters of the slots were simulated and optimized using Ansys HFSS electromagnetic simulation software. The simulation results yielded dual resonating frequency at 26 GHz and 30 GHz, with a reflection coefficient of $-25.87 \mathrm{~dB},-\mathbf{- 3 3. 5 3 \mathrm { dB }}$ and VSWR of $0.88 \mathrm{~dB}, \mathbf{0. 3 6} \mathrm{~dB}$ respectively, indicating excellent impedance matching. The antenna demonstrated a gain of $9.26 \mathrm{~dB}(11.4 \mathrm{dBi})$ and an operational bandwidth of 1.169 GHz at the 26.08 GHz resonance frequency. These performance metrics were achieved through the strategic incorporation of symmetrically arranged slots on the patch surface. The proposed slotted microstrip patch antenna design exhibits promising characteristics for deployment in next-generation radio communication systems operating in the mmWave frequency band, addressing the growing demand for high-performance antennas in this spectrum.

articleTitle: Integrated Modeling of Wireless System Performance under Beaulieu-Xie Fading and κ-μ Co-Channel Interference: A Multi-Dimensional Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper proposes simulation and analysis to discuss how the fading affects the wireless signal waves on different fading levels. Four types of fading: (i) no fading, (ii) a low level of fading, (iii) moderate level of fading and (iv), high level of fading was considered for simulating the signal amplitude over time. Selected fading levels were ‘added’ to model real world wireless scenarios in which both environmental and interference conditions are at play. The results indicated that in the absence of fading, the amplitude of the signal wave was continuous and not changed significantly; however, from low to severe fading, there could be directly proportional soaring fluctuations in its proper amplitude corresponding to lose of signal strength. Together, these findings underscore the importance of adaptive signal processing techniques and robust modulation strategies in suppressing the degradative effects of fading against the desirable characteristics of proper signal integrity and reliable performance. The findings highlight one reality in communications: understanding fading is critical for designing ultrareliable wireless systems that perform consistently across a variety of operational settings. The knowledge extracted based on this study would further add to novel way of designing robust strategies for Signal resilience and Communication reliability emerged in future wireless networks.

articleTitle: Blocking malicious domains: An experimental case study on DNS RPZ mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The Domain Name System (DNS) is a critical component of the internet infrastructure and is frequently targeted by attackers to distribute malware or for conducting phishing attacks. Cybercriminals are using malicious domains for various cyber attacks such as phishing, malware, ransomware, and other forms of cybercrime. The malicious domains are registered using fake identities or stolen identities, which makes it difficult to trace the attackers. The DNS Response Policy Zones (RPZ) mechanism is a security mechanism that allows organizations to block access to known malicious domains by responding to DNS queries with a non-existent IP address. This experimental case study evaluates the effectiveness of the DNS RPZ mechanism in blocking access to known malicious domains and reducing the number of malware infections and phishing attacks on client devices. The study was conducted using a BIND DNS server and a collection of known malware and phishing domains. The results show that the DNS RPZ mechanism was effective in blocking access to known malicious domains and reducing the number of malware infections and phishing attacks on the client devices. However, the study also highlights the need for future research to evaluate the scalability, real-world effectiveness, user behavior, and performance of the DNS RPZ mechanism in comparison with other security mechanisms.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Co-OFDMA: Performance in Overlapping Wi-Fi 6 Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper presents a design formulation and evaluation of a wireless co-OFDMA probabilistic algorithm aimed at optimizing resource utilization in overlapping Wi-Fi networks. The design formulation is grounded in realistic industrial application requirements, and the evaluation is conducted using the network simulator v3.0 with its DetNetWiFi module, which is capable of modeling deterministic wireless networks. The evaluation focuses on latency, jitter, and packet loss. Our findings demonstrate that co-OFDMA probabilistic approaches offer significant benefits in terms of latency in deterministic wireless environments. However, they may also introduce increased jitter compared to a static primary channel sharing scheme, aspect which may not be suitable to industrial wireless environments.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Local 5G Radio Estimation for Smart Factory Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper discusses advancements in smart factories using ICT and wireless communication, particularly focusing on minimal fabs, which are compact semiconductor facilities optimized for small-scale production. These fabs use 5G technology to enhance device interconnectivity and data exchange. The paper also explores Local 5G (L5G) networks in Japan, highlighting their application in environments requiring high confidentiality. Developers face challenges in optimizing wireless connectivity due to factors like building layout and obstructions. To address these challenges, the paper introduces a semi-automatically created database of factory layouts and a deep learning-based L5G radio estimation method, RadioResUNet, for predicting radio signal strength in smart factory environments. Additionally, we verify the radio estimation accuracy by comparing the practical L5G radio measurements conducted within the minimal fab.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed LSTM: Practical Vehicular Movement Projections in IoV
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper proposes a Physics-Informed Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model for predicting vehicular acceleration in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks. Current models are limited to linear motions; newer architectures explore merging the Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) with the LSTM model to leverage Physics-Informed Deep Learning Knowledge (PIDL). This study expands on previous work by incorporating nonlinear elements into the IDM. This work improves prediction accuracy and learning stability by comparing the performance of models with and without these nonlinear components. Experiments compared truncated versus padded/masked sequence processing of diverse human-driving data and 2D-IDM versus nonlinear IDM equations. Results indicate padded/masked sequences and nonlinear IDM equations provide more stable learning, though gradient explosions remain an issue. The model shows potential but requires further optimization before real-world deployment. This PIDL approach aims to balance the reliability of physics models with the flexibility of deep learning for improved vehicular acceleration prediction.

articleTitle: Resource and Power Allocation for Reliable 5G V2X Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) has transformed vehicular communication architecture by emphasising the need for reliable connections, high-capacity networks, and rapid message delivery within vehicular systems. This paper performs resource and power allocation to maximise the throughput of V2P and V2V users while maintaining the Quality-of-service ($\mathbf{Q o S}$) of cellular users (CUs) and V2I users. The maximisation problem is divided into two sub-problems to maximise the throughput of V2P and V2V users. To ensure reliable communication of V2P and V2V users, the expression for optimal power of V2P and V2V users is obtained using reliability constraints. The reuse matching problem is solved by Hungarian method to enhance the spectrum efficiency. The system performance is evaluated in terms of V2P throughput by varying number of CUs for different SINR threshold of CUs. Also, the throughput of V2V users is analysed by varying number of V2I users for different SINR threshold of V2I users. Furthermore, the proposed scheme is compared with an existing scheme in terms of throughput.

articleTitle: Implementation of Phased Array Antenna based on Multilayer fed with Substrate Integrated Waveguide Technology for Beam Scanning Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper introduces a multilayer-based substrate integrated waveguide-fed phased array antenna for targeting the next group of wireless communications, predominantly in Ku- and K-bands. The proposed work based on a hybrid structure utilizes a high-performance substrate-integrated waveguide feeding network, which facilitates the practical manufacturing of semi-circular microstrip patch antennas whereas dielectric substrates are printed on the circuit boards. The phased antenna array also comprises a printed periodic surface comprising ‘semi-circular’ type cells on an RT5880 dielectric substrate. As an outcome, the propped design reduces mutual coupling between parallel and 45° angular slots and phased array antenna configuration, results show a more compact array structure compared to other decoupling methods. Additionally, the proposed array antenna configuration has embraced a sixteen-element linearly phased array antenna with a wide angle beam with scanning competence. It shows that the phased array antenna scans the main lobe from -40° to $\mathbf{4 0}{ }^{\circ}$ and covers a frequency band from 18.12 to 19.67 GHz with input impedance bandwidth ($S_{11}{\lt}-10$ dB) of $\mathbf{8. 2 0 \%}\left(\mathrm{IBW}=1.55 \mathrm{GHz}, f_{c}=18.89 \mathrm{GHz}\right)$.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity LLR Detector for FrFT-IM-OFDM in the presence of ICI
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing with index modulation (IM-OFDM) combined with the fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) emerges as a cutting-edge multicarrier communication scheme, effectively reducing intercarrier interference (ICI) and surpassing traditional IM-OFDM systems in error performance. Traditional detection methods, such as maximum likelihood (ML) detection, are impractical for identifying the subcarrier activation pattern (SAP) due to their high computational demands. To address this challenge, we introduce a low complexity log-likelihood ratio (LLR) detector tailored for the FrFT-IM-OFDM system. This detector not only achieves performance comparable to the ML detector with significantly reduced complexity but also demonstrates a marked improvement in error performance over the fast Fourier transform (FFT)-IM-OFDM system equipped with an LLR detector, particularly in scenarios affected by carrier frequency offset (CFO). The bit error performance of the proposed LLR detector under ICI conditions underscores its potential for optimal IM-OFDM system implementations.

articleTitle: Research Issues and Challenges in AI-Embedded 6G Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: G will have extensive features of AI not only in providing AI-based services to users, but also in managing 6G networks making it more intelligent through its embedded AI tools. It will facilitate to implement AI-driven services using massive sensors and IoT devices. Native AI embedded in 6G network architecture will help optimize the spectrum, resources and performance in real-time. AI will make 6 G an autonomous network being self-organizing, self-healing and self-managed. The AI-driven applications are useful in sensing, industry automation, smart city and healthcare. We present the 6G network architecture for different sliced networks like sensing, IoT, distributed computing and satellite integrated 6G networks to identify different network operations that are to be managed by native AI. This also outlines the main technological challenges in 6 G and associated roles of AI for solutions. We present AI deployment scenarios based on various technological issues in 6G. Finally, we emphasize the importance of using appropriate AI tools specific 6 G issues giving examples of mapping between 6 G applications and recommended AI tools. We present the burning issues of AI implementation in 6G and challenges ahead. This work shall be useful for researchers to take up the issues and challenges for development of AI models and testify in the network for implementation.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of D2D Communication deployed in Uplink-mode B5G Cellular Network
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Device to Device communication feature in Next Generation communication networks helps develop small, localized network connecting large number of devices. It provides communication between the two devices that are in close vicinity without traversing data to any base station, thereby reducing the traffic load on base station, and improving overall network spectral efficiency using frequency-reuse. In this paper, we developed a mathematical model using stochastic geometry in uplink-mode. From the results it is clear that at low user densities transmission capacity is high and after reaching an optimal point, further increase in device-to-device density led to a paradoxical decline in transmission capacity. To ensure the validity of our theoretical model, we conducted an array of simulation experiments across a spectrum of device-to-device user densities.

articleTitle: Wearable Textile Antenna for GPS application
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The proposed wearable textile antenna has been designed for GPS (1.575 GHz) applications. Wearable textile antenna plays a vital role in Military applications. This GPS antenna has been specially designed for tracking the current location of the soldiers. The wearable antenna has been designed with textile material and a coplanar waveguide (CPW) feedline. The proposed antenna has been designed with simple structures, low profile, robustness, lightweight, and easy wear so that the soldiers can easily wear the uniform. The proposed antenna can be attached to the uniform so it becomes wearable. The current density of the proposed textile antenna has been evaluated. The proposed textile antenna has obtained a reflection coefficient of -16.17 dB, gain of 3.47 dBi, radiation efficiency of $\mathbf{9 7 \%}$ at 1.575 GHz frequency. It has been found that good agreement with the simulated results. The proposed wearable antenna has been designed on the CST microwave studio.

articleTitle: Integrating Machine Learning and IoT for Frozen Shoulder Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In recent years, Internet of medical things (IoMT) has gained a lot of interest in research. Frozen shoulder is a serious muscular condition which restricts the movement of shoulder muscles of the patient. In this paper, the state of the art technologies in the field of physical rehabilitation to offer remote rehabilitation services tailored for individuals recovering from frozen shoulder conditions is first discussed. The system proposed and developed in this work comprises accelerometer, gyroscope sensors, and a microprocessor board connected to Microsoft Azure cloud via Wi-Fi. The system employs a convolution neural network trained for five different exercises to classify and recognize various movements. Furthermore, the paper discusses the implementation of wearable sensors to capture biomechanical data during rehabilitation exercises, providing real-time feedback to both the patient and healthcare provider. The integration of the developed system with internet enables remote monitoring and supervision, allowing for personalized exercise prescription and adjustment based on individual progress and needs. This remote rehabilitation system offers a convenient and cost-effective solution to improve accessibility to rehabilitation services, particularly for individuals with limited mobility or residing in remote areas.

articleTitle: O-RAN Based User Tracking for Emergency Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Accurate user localization in cellular networks is critical, especially during emergencies. This paper proposes a method using Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) technology to enhance real-time user tracking within emergency zones. By leveraging the Near-Real-Time Radio Intelligent Controller (near-RT RIC) and xApps, the suggested approach tracks user movements through handover messages across base stations, improving emergency response effectiveness. Simulations validate the method’s potential, highlighting its ability to address challenges in traditional localization techniques.

articleTitle: Information Rate For Molecular Communication Over Super Diffusive Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In this paper, we study the communication between two bio-nanomachines consisting of cluster of biological entities such as genetically modified bacteria, where data is denoted by the concentration of the transmitted molecules. Further, the molecules produced by the transmitter bio-nanomachine propagate through the super diffusive channel. Then, the concentration of molecules is detected in the receiver bio-nanomachine by certain molecules and respond accordingly. Our work explores the theoretical limitations of information transmission rates in the presence of uncertainty. Moreover, to measure the information rate per unit time the delay introduced by both channel and reception process should be considered. Specifically, the time taken for the concentration of molecules to achieve stable state at the receiver, bacteria to decode the concentration of molecules, and channel readiness for transmission of the next sample will be computed. To account for channel delays, the rise time and fall time of the channel’s diffusion process will be determined.

articleTitle: Enhancing Communication for the Hearing Impaired: A Real-Time Speech to Sign Language Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Whether it’s conversing, playing computer games, attending a meeting, or participating in a video conference, deaf individuals constantly miss out on the enjoyment that other people may have. Since not every local speaks sign language, communicating with them is the hardest issue. The goal of our research is to develop a communication system for the deaf by converting words or speech into sign language.
