The system records voice, translates it into text, and displays Indian Sign Language actions application serves a dual function by not only translating English speech into textual representation but also into visual formats with appropriate Sign language counterpart of the word/alphabet. The uniqueness of its predictive analysis model lies in its ability to process frames over a 5 -second duration, generating cumulative sentences that are synthesized into video, enhancing accessibility for a diverse user base. Furthermore, the SignLingo extends its inclusivity by providing a valuable service to individuals with visual impairments. The synergistic combination of advanced machine learning techniques with an intuitive and user-centric interface positions the sign language conversion as a pioneering initiative in creating truly inclusive communication spaces.

articleTitle: Enhancing Network Security: A Modular Neural Network Approach to Detect Suspicious Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The increasing complexity and sophistication of cyber threats pose significant challenges to network security. Detecting suspicious patterns in network traffic-such as unusual activity, unexpected communications, and atypical data patterns—is critical for identifying potential cyber-attacks and unauthorized network use. In this study, we propose a modular neural network approach, integrating Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Nonlinear AutoRegressive eXogenous (NARX) models, to effectively detect these anomalies. The modular structure divides the problem into manageable subproblems, allowing for enhanced accuracy and flexibility. The RNN’s ability to process sequential data, combined with the NARX model’s capacity to capture both internal and external dependencies, makes this hybrid approach particularly effective in analyzing complex network traffic patterns. We trained and tested the proposed model using both typical and atypical network traffic data, achieving a mean squared error close to zero during the training phase. This research contributes to the development of more resilient and adaptive cybersecurity solutions, capable of safeguarding networks against evolving threats.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Polarization Converting Metasurface for Enhanced 5G and wi-fi Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band polarization converting metasurface to enhance the signal quality and network efficiency of the $\mathbf{n 7 8}$ band and the $5 \mathbf{~ G H z}$ band of wi-fi. This proposed dual-band polarization converting metasurface (PCM) behaves as a reflective-type linear-to-cross polarization converter with a minimum 80% polarization conversion ratio (PCR) over the frequency bands of $(3.37-3.54) \mathbf{~ G H z}$ and $(4.95-5.07) \mathbf{~ G H z}$. On the other hand, for a linearly polarized incident wave on the PCM, the reflected wave would be circularly polarized for the frequency bands of $3.32-3.34 \mathbf{~ G H z}, 3.53-3.56 \mathbf{G H z}, 4.84-4.92$ GHz and $5.10-5.20 \mathbf{~ G H z}$. The PCM unit cell consists of two diagonally placed nonagon-shaped rings joined by a microstrip line on the top of a metal-backed Rogers RT5870 substrate. The unit cell is compact with periodicity $0.17 \lambda_{0} \times 0.17 \lambda_{0}$ and low profile with a thickness of $0.018 \lambda_{0}$. The proposed PCM has remarkable potential and capacity in creating intelligent reflecting surfaces to substantially enhance coverage and elevate the performance of $\mathbf{5 G}$ and wi-fi networks.

articleTitle: Enhancing Drone Efficiency with 5G-Enabled Cloud-Based Processing for Real-Time Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Drones have emerged as indispensable tools across various sectors, yet their operational range remains hindered by battery limitations. To overcome this difficulty, an innovative strategy for reducing energy use through cloud-based processing is presented in this study. Our approach makes use of a Raspberry Pi-5 as a client that is mounted on the drone followed by a camera that takes pictures on a fixed interval. Rather than analyzing the visual data locally, which can quickly deplete the drone’s battery, it is sent to Google Drive for cloud-based analysis. Using the fast data transfer speed of $5 \mathrm{G} \mathrm{Wi-Fi}$ a server gets these images on a regular interval and uses the YOLOv8-L object detection model for real-time analysis, mainly focusing on human detection along with their common vehicles to improve the detection. By employing this approach, it not only increases the drones’ surveillance time but also provide a workable and expandable way to improve their capabilities while using less battery power. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the integration of Raspberry Pi-5, visual sensor (camera), cloud storage, and server systems, showcasing the seamless flow of data and processing tasks enabled by 5G-based Wi-Fi. Our results demonstrate significant improvements in operational efficiency and highlight the potential for widespread adoption of cloud-based processing in drone technology.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization versus Simulated Annealing for 5G and 6G Wireless Networks: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The evolution from 5G to 6G represents a significant leap in wireless communication technology, moving beyond enhanced mobile broadband, low latency, and increased connectivity offered by 5G. The evolution of 5G is expected to create a whole new way to connect and communicate around the world. In this paper, we compare the performance of Particle Swarm Optimization PSO and Simulated Annealing SA in optimizing network density and network interference in 5G and6G wireless networks, focusing on the technological advancements and challenges associated with the transition. PSO is a more effective optimization algorithm than SA across multiple dimensions of network performance, particularly in the challenging context of 6G networks, where the demands for optimization are greater. These results underscore PSO’s potential to significantly enhance network performance in the complex, dense environments of next-generation wireless systems. It is crucial to focus on sustainable and energy-efficient solutions to support the anticipated massive increase in connected devices and data traffic, ensuring that the technological advances are matched with responsible development practices.

articleTitle: Designing Of Hybrid Intrusion Detection System With Combined Approach Of LightGBM-AE And Double DQN
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Cyber-attacks are a growing threat to individuals, businesses, and governments. Data science helps improve security by analyzing network traffic and system activities. Intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are essential for enhancing security and resilience, but IDS datasets face challenges in obtaining quality training data and accurately predicting cyberattacks. To tackle these issues, this paper designs a novel hybrid intrusion detection system that detects malicious behavior based on signature and anomaly. It utilizes advanced techniques like one hot encoding, min-max normalization for data preprocessing, modified GAMO for data oversampling, information gain, and modified grey wolf optimizer (GWO)based bi-phase approach for feature selection, stacking of LightGBM with autoencoder for signature-based detection, and finally double deep Q-network (Double DQN) for anomaly-based detection to create robust and efficient hybrid IDS model. The proposed model achieves $\mathbf{9 4. 3 3 \%}$ and $\mathbf{8 8. 9 0 \%}$ accuracy utilizing signature-based and anomaly-based IDS, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art “MTH-HIDS” in accuracy, precision, recall, and f1-score.

articleTitle: Pre-Harvest to Post-Harvest: A Review of AI and IoT Applications in Smart Agriculture and the Prospects of 6G-Enabled IoT Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Farmers are increasingly adopting Smart farming worldwide, leveraging various advanced technologies. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is instrumental in driving the evolution of smart agriculture applications. Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, cloud computing, and big data are among the forefront technologies employed in this field. Agricultural activities typically encompass three phases: pre-harvest, during harvest, and postharvest. The pre-harvest phase involves choosing seeds, preparing the farm, and selecting the crops. Harvesting tasks include crop classification, disease analysis, and pathogen detection. Post-harvesting activities involve storage, cooling, and reaping, among others. This study conducted an in-depth review of activities in each phase, aiming at shortcomings related to AI-based Machine and Deep learning, IoT, security, datasets, and methodologies employed in existing research. This work also proposes a smart farming framework based on 6G technology, utilizing these identified research gaps. Additionally, the work conducted a comparative analysis between this survey and existing studies, revealing that the survey offers a more comprehensive overview in various aspects.

articleTitle: Tweeting the Pulse: Unveiling Sentiments on India’s new Education Policy
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In today’s digital age, where social media platforms play a pivotal role in public discourse, it is essential to gauge sentiments towards major policy initiatives. This project focuses on analyzing Twitter data to explore public sentiment regarding India’s Education Policy of 2020. The goal is to develop a machine learning-based sentiment analysis model specifically designed for tweets about educational policies in India. By categorizing tweets as positive, negative, or neutral, the project aims to reveal public attitudes and perceptions toward the policy. The model integrates domain-specific knowledge and advanced natural language processing techniques to enhance the precision and relevance of sentiment analysis within the context of educational policy discussions. Ultimately, the project aspires to provide policymakers and stakeholders with meaningful insights derived from social media, thereby supporting informed decision-making and encouraging more active public participation in educational reforms.

articleTitle: Water Quality Index Prediction Using Modified LSTM-GAN Model Towards Sustainable Urban Development
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Rivers are major source of fresh water. However, urbanization is severely polluting fresh water bodies, posing serious risks to life. To handle this challenge, the proposed model predicts Water Quality Index (WQI), which is an amalgamation of GAN (Generative Adversarial Network) and modified LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) with connected memory. The GAN model is used in the pre-processing stage for intensive missing value imputation and data scaling is performed for error minimization. Further, in the prediction stage preprocessed dataset passed to LSTM with connected memory that merges input and forget gate to reduce complexity. The memory cell directly connected to the gates of modified model with added intelligence. The proposed model demonstrates superior performance over compatible existing baseline models achieving higher efficiency in terms of Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) by 0.0998 and 0.0977 respectively. Moreover, the R-square value shows slight increase of 0.998.

articleTitle: Achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by Leveraging 6G Services
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are basically the framework for ensuring better humanity, society, environment and equality by removing poverty and hunger. An extensive study, review, analysis and recommendation on various aspects such as human life & constraints, and societal & environmental issues are essential to make an effective and productive plan to achieve the benchmarks of SDGs. 6G technology is expected to provide converged fast data communication and edge computing. AI enabled 6 G will also provide extensive services on sensory information related to human, animal and environment with almost 100% coverage on earth and sky. Thus, 6G has potential to excel the achievement of SDGs through its pervasive information acquisition, AI based analysis, and continuous monitoring of the status in real time. In this article, we explore key enablers for SDG that are essential for implementation. We relate those enablers with the 6G service applications. This helps understand how 6G services are to be leveraged for SDG to accelerate progress and make a better world. Further, we suggest a virtual network on 6G platform and SDG control entity with signaling to monitor the status and execute the plans for SDGs.

articleTitle: Unraveling Mental Health Trends: Predictive Insights Through NLP Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Mental health is a critical aspect of overall well-being, yet it often remains underdiagnosed and untreated due to stigma, lack of awareness, and limited access to resources. With the increasing availability of digital communication platforms, there is a growing body of textual data that reflects individuals’ thoughts, emotions, and experiences. Leveraging this data through advanced computational techniques such as Natural Language Processing (NLP) offers a novel approach to understanding and predicting mental health status. By analyzing language patterns in text, NLP can provide insights into an individual’s mental state, potentially enabling early detection and timely intervention. This paper explores the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) for predicting mental health status from textual data. Employing decision trees, it analyzes linguistic patterns to classify individuals ’ mental health conditions. Testing and evaluation on diverse datasets reveal promising results, indicating the potential of NLP-based approaches for early detection and intervention in mental health disorders. The study underscores the importance of leveraging NLP techniques in healthcare for improving mental health outcomes and facilitating personalized interventions.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Large Intelligent Surfaces Assisted NOMA Network for 5G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Large intelligent surfaces (LIS) assisted nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) networks is a promising technology for 5 G and beyond network. In this work, we have completed the performance analysis of LIS supported NOMA network. We have proposed a system model where multiple users are served by a gNB/base station (BS) equipped with LIS. In this work, our focus is on downlink scenario where the BS simultaneously transmits to multiple users using NOMA and, the LIS helps to increase the received signal quality as well as coverage. Later, we have analyzed the performance of the proposed LIS-assisted NOMA network and compared with conventional NOMA systems without LISs. The results showed that the LIS can significantly improve the system performance regarding probability of error, pairwise error probability (PEP) and diversity gain. It is observed that error probability is reduced from approximately $10^{-3}$ to $10^{-6}$ with M = 2 to $M=5$ at a signal-to-noise (SNR) of around 21 dB. Such findings would provide a valuable insight into LIS-assisted NOMA networks which is a part of 5 G and 6 G networks.

articleTitle: Resource Optimization for RIS-Assisted D2D Communication in 5G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In the era of 5G and beyond, the demand for high data rates, enhanced security, and precise localization continues to grow, driven by advanced services. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a transformative technology for optimizing wireless environments. This paper explores the integration of RIS with device-to-device (D2D) communication to improve resource utilization in dense network settings. The study focuses on maximizing the overall sum-rate for cellular users (CUs) and D2D multicast groups within a RIS-assisted system. We employ a joint optimization approach encompassing active beamforming at the base station (BS), RIS phase shifts, and channel allocation. To address the complex optimization problem, we propose an iterative algorithm with a closed-form solution and a weighted bipartite matching algorithm for channel allocation, implemented via the Hungarian method. Results demonstrate notable improvements in sum-rate for both CUs and D2D multicast groups, highlighting thepromise of RIS-assisted D2D communication for future wireless networks.

articleTitle: NSSF Function in 6G Networks Based on MLOps Deployment Model
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: 6G networks present new challenges as a platform for innovation in network management, particularly regarding the Network Slice Selection Function (NSSF) in heterogeneous environments. Current approaches have been implemented gradually, highlighting the need for new methodologies for slice selection and orchestration. The NSSF framework in 6G networks uses Intelligent Edge Computing, MLOps, and Artificial Intelligence for IT Operations (AIOps) in cloud-native architectures. This framework integrates RAN, Edge, and Core networks offering a scalable solution aligned with 3GPP TS 29.531 standards. It’s design is based on divide-and-conquer models, promoting management via OPEX/CAPEX and optimizing QoS/QoE through slicing techniques. The proposed solution was tested using a combination of open-source NFV tools and continuous integration pipelines, ensuring interoperability between domains. Initial testing suggests the framework can enhance E2E orchestration in 6G networks while addressing key performance indicators (KPIs) for AI, ML, and zero-touch network management. Future work will further explore the framework’s adaptability to different use cases.

articleTitle: Mitigating Advanced Persistent Threats using a Combinational Algorithm of Semi-Supervised Support Vector Machines and Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The S3VM-GCN model is crucial for 6G networks due to its ability to efficiently detect and mitigate security threats in highly complex, dynamic environments. 6G networks will rely heavily on vast IoT ecosystems and edge computing, making them vulnerable to coordinated attacks. The semi-supervised S3VM component enhances detection by leveraging both labeled and un-labeled data, which is essential given the scarcity of labeled attack data in real-world 6G scenarios. To identify the malicious nodes in 6G network TON IoT standard database is used as reference for IoT network intrusions. Meanwhile, the GCN component effectively models the intricate relationships between devices in 6G networks, allowing for more accurate detection of compromised nodes and real-time adaptation to evolving threats. The combination can provide a powerful and scalable security solution based on the demanding needs of 6G. An integrated approach to graph convolutional networks and semi-supervised support vector machines for enhancement in the detection and analysis of attacks against IoT is proposed in this paper. Simulating different coordinated attack scenarios against IoT devices through a network graph built from real-world telemetry data and network traffic. This approach involves preprocessing the data, building a graph-based representation of the network, and using GCN for deep learning-based classification. Simultaneously, S3VM is employed to leverage unlabeled data, improving classification accuracy. In the testing process, the proposed model was run against standard metrics and proved to be effective in compromised node identification and network vulnerability visualization. This work thus contributes toward IoT security by providing a robust method for detecting and mitigating network-based attacks.

Author Keywords: Coordinated Attacks Via Compromised IOT devices

articleTitle: Navigating Privacy in the Data Economy
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: The data economy is revolutionizing how organizations leverage information to drive innovation, optimize operations, and create value. With data as a pivotal asset, navigating privacy regulations like GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, HIPAA, and DPDPA has become increasingly complex. This paper examines the effects of these growing regulations and their implications for multinational businesses, addressing the legal and operational challenges of cross-country data exchange. Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PETs) are highlighted as essential tools for compliance and consumer data protection, enabling legitimate data use. The dual nature of data-as a valuable enterprise asset and a potential individual risk if mishandled-is underscored. Best practices for balancing data-driven innovation with robust privacy measures are explored, offering organizations a roadmap for managing critical individual data. Through comprehensive analysis, this paper aims to equip stakeholders with the necessary technological solutions to harness the data economy’s potential while ensuring strict adherence to privacy regulations and mitigating individual privacy risks.

articleTitle: ROS-Lighthouse: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) in ROS using Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Security concerns of Robot Operating System (ROS) have come to the limelight recently, especially as ROS is paving its way into more applications. ROS lacks built-in security features in its architecture, rendering it susceptible to attacks. Efforts have been made to secure ROS communication; however, the current landscape still poses risks. This study proposes ROSlighthouse, a framework based on machine learning, that probes through the data received by a ROS node to classify intrusions. An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is created utilizing the Super Learner algorithm to identify intrusions within ROS networks. ROS-lighthouse has been assessed and determined to detect intrusions with accuracies up to 99.907%. Additionally, recommendations and future directions for enhancing ROSlighthouse’s connectivity to the internet are provided.

articleTitle: Multi-Layer Resource Management Strategies for Cybernetic Avatars in Dynamic Local 5G Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: Cybernetic Avatars (CAs) are envisioned to revolutionize society by extending human physical and cognitive capabilities through advanced ICT and robotics, as part of Japan’s Moonshot Goal 1 project. CAs are technologies that extend human physical and cognitive capabilities, enabling remote activities and offering a new means for anyone to participate in social activities. However, when a large number of CAs operate simultaneously, service quality is impaired due to limited wireless communication capacity. To address this issue, this study proposes a wireless resource management scheme in a dynamic Local 5G network environment. This scheme manages the available service areas for each CA service in a multi-layer structure and adaptively downgrades the service levels of some CAs when communication demands exceed the available capacity. This approach ensures that, in scenarios where communication resources are strained due to a high number of CAs, service levels can be effectively adjusted based on the CAs’ situations and operations, maintaining the overall service quality at a higher level. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly improves the proportion of CAs meeting the desired quality of service compared to the conventional Proportional Fair Scheduling (PFS)-based resource management scheme. These results indicate that even under limited resource conditions, it is possible to maintain high service quality.

articleTitle: Credit Card Eligibility Prediction Using ML
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: In the finance sector, particularly in developing countries with high fraud rates, struggle to approve Creditcard applications accurately while reducing fraud risk. This research explores how Machine learning helps to overcome this problem. The goal of this research is to reduce potential futurecredit risk that could help the bank’s financial health and creditperformance by applying machine learning (ML) techniques to anticipate a customer’s eligibility for a credit card. A creditcard is a line of credit extended to a consumer by banks and finance organizations worldwide. The banks and financialinstitutions are exposed to credit risk via the credit facility. Repayments are not guaranteed, and the loan frequently becomes non-performing. Before extending a loan facility, banks evaluate applicant’s creditworthiness and eligibility in an effort to reduce credit risk. Since credit worthiness is largely determined bytraditional credit scoring techniques, it is not always reliable. Wego with traditional models like Logistic regression and decision trees by comparatively analyzing their effectiveness in predicting credit card approvals. The classifiers that are available here are SGD, Logistic Regression, SVC, Gaussian NB and K Neighbours. These models analyze past data to identify patterns indicative of fraudulent activity, significantly improving credit cardapproval process security. This combined approach goes beyond just boosting accuracy. It paves the way for a more inclusive and secure financial landscape in developing economies. By combining traditional ML techniques with specialized fraud detection models, this study provides a strong foundation for a responsible and effective credit card approval process that fosters financial inclusion while combating fraudulent activities.

articleTitle: Advances and Adaptation in Artificial General Intelligence Based on Novel Q* Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 27th International Symposium on Wireless Personal Multimedia Communications (WPMC)
abstract: A priority in the researches on artificial intelligence is the creation of Artificial General Intelligence. Even though the regular artificial intelligence was making some progress in certain areas, there were challenges and untried domains. This study introduces a novel $Q^{*}$ framework which is intended for improving AGI. Understanding, obtaining and using machine-generated knowledge across multiple domains are some of the aspects of AGI. It integrates concepts form cognitive psychology and reinforcement learning to produces a cohesive approach that includes learning as well as introspection and flexibility. By leveraging the advantages of Q-learning and refining existing methods, achieving AGI through $\mathbf{Q}^{*}$ is feasible. $\mathbf{Q}^{*}$ prioritizes metalearning and hierarchical representations over traditional AI systems that perform well within narrow contexts yet fail when asked to generalize more broadly. This makes it possible to be adaptable and learn well in unfamiliar settings. The paper gives a detailed explanation of the theoretical underpinnings and possible applications of AGI, emphasizing $Q^{* \prime}$ ‘s commitmentto advancing its pursuit. We discuss the conceptual framework proposed by Q* $^{*}$ and speculate on its implications for future AI research.
